what_this_is: One review harness, three rule weightings. The three apps are three different
problems: reso-landing-app is a purchased marketing template, so its token
conformance is someone else's design system and the live question is whether the
page WORKS; reso-management-app is a design-system app, where conformance is the
whole job and the deterministic layer does nearly all of it, so the model's budget
goes to what no rule can reach; reso-web-app sits between.
These are POLICY, not measurement. Nothing in this file asserts a fact about a
checkout -- no framework version, no token-source path treated as present. Per the
spec's C11 ruling, a table that bans prose as a source must be GENERATED, and the
generator (profiles.json from a live repo read) is not built here. The one field
that would carry such a fact, `token_source`, is a PROBE to run against the repo,
and until it is run the router reports coverage.dom as partial rather than letting

t2_classes.hierarchy: relative visual weight across a whole frame; the DOM has no such relation
t2_classes.gestalt: grouping is proximity + similarity + enclosure interacting; each is measurable, their resolution is not
t2_classes.content-fit: whether a caption's promise matches the render is a language-to-pixel comparison
t2_classes.semantic-coherence: an unlabelled control is valid HTML with a valid AX tree; the defect is that a human cannot tell what it does
t2_classes.optical-alignment: geometric centre is not optical centre; the compensation is deliberate and its absence is a judgement
t2_classes.readability: left-aligned numerics are geometrically perfect and read wrong

why: A purchased template's token conformance is a measurement of somebody else's
design system. Reporting drift against tokens the team never chose spends the
reviewer's credibility on findings nobody will action -- and credibility is the
resource the ~20% false-positive cliff actually meters. So the conformance
families stay ON (a silently disabled rule is a blind spot that reads like a
clean report) and drop to ADVISORY: reported, never gating, never winning the
page's one region call against a contrast or overflow finding.
Conformance is the whole job here and the deterministic layer does nearly all
of it, so the model's budget goes to what rules cannot reach at all. That is
why per_page_max is 1, not a budget cut: the residue after the screen and the
cross-check is smallest precisely where the screen is strongest, and a page
here needing a second region call is a page whose RULES are missing -- the
second finding is the signal to file that, not an image to buy.
The token families carry full weight, and the one thing that must not happen is
a confident FAIL whose truth value depends on which of two engines resolved the
declaration. Where a token map cannot be resolved the class ABSTAINS, which
routes; it does not pass, which routes nowhere.

token_source.note: a multi-engine PostCSS chain needs an explicit precedence before any token class may assert; without one the class abstains

why: No emphasis is asserted because none is measured. All six T2 classes are asked
unweighted, which is the honest default for an app whose conformance surface
has not been established. Runtime-hashed class names are not invertible, so a
token-conformance finding here cannot name a source site; that is an
attribution limit, and it is a reason to abstain rather than to guess.
The instrument's own profile, so a router run over the corpus is not silently
borrowing an app's weighting. Everything neutral, every class asked.
